t: Founded around 1336 by the Sangama brothers on the Tungabhadra as Delhi Sultanate power collapsed in the south.
Under Krishnadevaraya (r. 1509–1529) it was the dominant power of southern India, ruled from a vast capital at Hampi.
Defeat at Talikota in 1565 led to the sack of the capital; nayaka governors became independent and the empire ended by 1646.
dyk: The site of Madras, where the English built Fort St George in 1639–40, was granted by a local nayaka who served the Aravidu kings of Vijayanagara.
ev: Harihara I and Bukka I found the kingdom on the Tungabhadra
The Madurai Sultanate is destroyed by Vijayanagara armies
Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq visits the capital
Krishnadevaraya defeats Bijapur at the Battle of Raichur
The Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara at Talikota and sack the capital
Tirumala founds the Aravidu dynasty at Penukonda
Sriranga III loses his last territories to Bijapur and Golconda

f.capital: Vijayanagara (Hampi); later Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore
f.predecessor: Hoysala Empire; Delhi Sultanate (in the south)
f.successor: Nayaka kingdoms (Madurai, Thanjavur, Gingee), Kingdom of Mysore, Bijapur and Golconda sultanates
